relations.subject: capella:query-tab

relations.subject: capella:query-tab
relations.evidence: To view the Query tab and run queries that _read_ documents, you need the [Data Reader](../../projects/project-roles.md#project-cluster-data-reader) project role.

relations.subject: capella:query-tab
relations.evidence: To run queries that read and modify documents, you need the [Project Owner](../../projects/project-roles.md#project-owner-role) or [Data Writer](../../projects/project-roles.md#project-cluster-data-reader-writer) role.

relations.subject: capella:query-tab
relations.evidence: To run queries that read and modify documents, you need the [Project Owner](../../projects/project-roles.md#project-owner-role) or [Data Writer](../../projects/project-roles.md#project-cluster-data-reader-writer) role.

relations.subject: capella:query-tab
relations.evidence: **Support for SQL++ INFER statements**: Support the SQL++ [INFER](../../n1ql/n1ql-language-reference/infer.md) statement.

relations.subject: capella:query-tab
relations.evidence: The [ADVISE](../../n1ql/n1ql-language-reference/advise.md) command generates index advice to recommend indexes that optimize the response time for a query.

relations.subject: capella:query-tab
relations.evidence: Each time you execute a query, an [EXPLAIN](../../n1ql/n1ql-language-reference/explain.md) command is automatically run in the background to retrieve the query plan for that query.

relations.subject: capella:query-tab
relations.evidence: In the query editor, write a SQL++ query or use [Capella iQ](../../get-started/capella-iq/work-with-capellaiq.md) for assistance.

relations.subject: capella:iq-insights
relations.evidence: The **iQ Insights** tab lets you leverage the power of AI to generate relevant questions, descriptions, and visualizations of your query results.

notable_absence.finding: No Enterprise/Community edition badges and no server-version-string citations appear anywhere on this page - consistent with the pattern that Capella's own UI-procedural pages (as opposed to the underlying SQL++ statement reference pages they link to) generally omit both known recurring anomalies.

cross_component_finding: Confirms reuse over minting: the Query tab is documented as a thin browser client over the pre-existing Query Service and pre-existing SQL++ statement family (INFER, ADVISE, EXPLAIN, LIMIT) rather than introducing its own query language or execution model. The only genuinely new concepts on this page are UI-surface features layered on top - Query Settings (Max Parallelism, Transaction Timeout, Scan Consistency - all pass-through cbq-engine/request-level parameters, not new primitives) and iQ Insights, an AI-result-visualization surface for Capella iQ that doesn't exist in the underlying SQL++ execution model at all.
